How to do itHammer Curl

Elbow path

Right
ELBOWS AT SIDES
Wrong
ELBOWS FORWARD

Right: Elbows by the sides at the top.

Wrong: Elbows pushed forward, dumbbells lifted by the shoulders.

Keep the palms facing your body from bottom to top. No wrist twist.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows forwardYour elbows move forward as the dumbbells come up.
  2. Shoulder takes overThe front of your shoulder takes the load instead of the biceps.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Closed neutral grip, thumbs round the handles. Wrist straight, palms facing your body.

Keep the wrist from twisting through the lift.

Common handling mistakes

  • Elbows moving forward or back

    Fix: Keep the elbows at your sides.

  • Wrists twisting out of neutral

    Fix: Keep the palms facing your body the whole way.

  • Swinging the body

    Fix: Take weight off and lift with control.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arm and your forearm.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour elbows move forward, which loads the front delts.

    FixKeep the elbows at your sides.

  • Usually meansYour wrist is bending or twisting.

    FixKeep the wrist straight, palms facing your body.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pick dumbbells you can curl without swinging.

  2. 2

    Take a split stance, brace, shoulders down and back.

  3. 3

    Hold the dumbbells with a closed neutral grip beside your thighs.

  4. 4

    Curl to the front of the shoulders, lower to straight arms.

  5. 5

    Torso upright, no arching the lower back, no shrugging.

Risks and when to stop

  • Too heavy a weight can make you swing and cut reps short.
  • Elbows moving forward put extra load on the front delts.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

TORSO UPRIGHT

Right: Torso upright, lower back not arched. Resting arm hangs straight.

Wrong: Trunk moving as the dumbbell swings up.

Keep the resting arm hanging in the start position.

Grip

Palms forward, thumbs wrapped round the handles.

Keep the hand in line with the forearm, not bent up or down.

Common handling mistakes

  • Wrist bending up or down

    Fix: Keep the hand in line with the forearm.

  • Elbow swinging forward or back

    Fix: Keep the elbow close to your torso.

  • Swinging the body

    Fix: Use a lighter dumbbell and lift with control.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arm.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour wrists are bent up or down under load.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Keep the wrist straight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pick dumbbells light enough to curl without swinging.

  2. 2

    Stand in a split stance, torso braced, shoulders down and back.

  3. 3

    Palms-forward grip, thumbs round the handles, arms at your sides.

  4. 4

    Curl one arm while the other stays down. Lower before switching.

  5. 5

    Curl to the front of the shoulder, lower to a straight arm.

Risks and when to stop

  • Bent wrists under load can cause wrist discomfort.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Elbow path

Right
ELBOW AT SIDE

Right: Upper arms by the sides at the top.

Keep the upper arms by your body. Never let them travel back.

Grip

Underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width, thumbs wrapped.

Keep the hands in line with the forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Wrists bending

    Fix: Keep the hands in line with the forearms.

  • Elbows travelling back or forward

    Fix: Keep the upper arms at your sides.

  • Swinging the body

    Fix: Take weight off and lift with control.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your upper arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour elbows move forward, which loads the front delts.

    FixKeep the upper arms at your sides.

  • Usually meansYour wrists are bent up or down under load.

    FixStop and don't train through the pain. Keep the wrist straight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pick a weight you can curl without swinging.

  2. 2

    Stand with your feet hip-width, core braced.

  3. 3

    Grip the bar underhand, hands shoulder-width.

  4. 4

    Keep your chest and body still. Only your arms move.

  5. 5

    Lower the bar slowly, keeping tension at the bottom. No half reps.

Risks and when to stop

  • Bent wrists put extra load on them and can lead to discomfort, even injury.

Wrist pain

Grip

Overhand grip, palms down, hands about shoulder-width.

Keep the wrists neutral, in line with the forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging to move the bar

    Fix: Go lighter and control both the lift and the lowering.

  • Wrists bending under the bar

    Fix: Keep the wrists neutral.

  • Elbows flaring outward

    Fix: Reduce the weight. Keep the elbows close to your ribs.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your forearms and the front of your upper arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour wrist is bending.

    FixKeep the wrist neutral, in line with the forearm.

  • Usually meansYou swing the bar up with momentum.

    FixGo lighter and slow down.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Start light. Add weight as you get stronger.

  2. 2

    Stand with feet hip- to shoulder-width, knees soft.

  3. 3

    Grip the bar overhand, hands about shoulder-width.

  4. 4

    Stand tall, no arching. Shoulders back and down, chin slightly tucked.

  5. 5

    Lower the bar slowly, keeping tension at the bottom.

Risks and when to stop

  • Swinging a weight above your ability could hurt your joints.
  • Bent wrists add strain to the wrists.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Elbow pain

Severe pain and hard to move, heard a snap, changed shape, tingling, or numbness? Get it checked today.
